# A package const a free function reads is the file-scope name, on every
# target.
#
# A list const is not folded into its readers, so the Go targets declare it:
# a field of the Model, read through the receiver inside a method, and a
# file-scope `var`, read by name in a function that is no method. `rank`
# reads nothing of the Model and is written as a free function, but from the
# package body's scope, which spelled the const `m.fruits` in a function with
# no `m`. bubbletea declared the file-scope `var`; fyne and gtk4 declared none.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

const fruits = ["apple", "fig", "pear"]

// Where `name` comes among the fruits, or after them all.
func rank(name string) int {
    for var i, f = fruits {
        if f == name {
            return i
        }
    }
    return fruits.length()
}

component main ui.node {
    var pick = "fig"

    ui.text(value="{rank(pick)}")
}

func testRanks(t test.Test, c main) {
    t.assert(rank(c.pick) == 1)
    t.assert(rank("kiwi") == 3)
}
